summary: Negotiations to end the U.S.-Iran war show progress with Qatari mediators in Tehran and an Iranian response expected by the weekend. IDF and Shin Bet destroyed two Hamas weapons warehouses in Al-Bureij and Gaza City containing RPGs, rockets, Kalashnikovs, and explosives. An Israeli soldier was indicted for espionage for Iran, passing sensitive military information including base coordinates and interceptors for cryptocurrency.
key_points: Qatari mediators delivered revised proposals to Tehran Friday as U.S.-Iran war negotiations advance toward a weekend Iranian response. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/9110)
IDF and Shin Bet struck two Hamas weapons warehouses in Al-Bureij and Gaza City, eliminating stockpiles of RPGs, rockets, Kalashnikovs, grenades, and explosives. (Source: @N12chat/232486)

Israeli soldier arrested and charged with year-long espionage for Iran, providing military base coordinates, interceptor details, and comrade identities for cryptocurrency payments. (Source: @manniefabian/59453)
U.S. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper presented military strike options on Iran to President Trump with Defense Secretary and Joint Chiefs Chair attending. (Source: @yediotnews25/137034)
Lebanese Army conducted controlled explosion in Barish, Ain al-Ramouh area between 12:30-13:30 local time. (Source: @redlinkleb/50580)
Artillery shelling reported in Wadi al-Saluqi near Toulene and Wadi al-Hajir in southern Lebanon. (Source: @redlinkleb/50589, @redlinkleb/50569)

Flydubai suspended all flights to Israel until November 30 amid regional tensions. (Source: @yediotnews25/137048)

sections.threat_assessment: The convergence of advancing U.S.-Iran diplomacy and simultaneous Iranian missile testing signals a dual-track strategy: Tehran seeks leverage through demonstrated military capability while exploring diplomatic off-ramps. The Israeli soldier espionage case reveals persistent Iranian intelligence penetration targeting IDF operational readiness and personnel, with cryptocurrency enabling covert payments. Hamas weapons cache destruction in Gaza degrades immediate tactical capabilities but the Shin Bet's direct outreach to operatives suggests a shift toward targeted dismantlement of leadership networks. Lebanese border artillery activity and electronic surveillance in Dahiyeh indicate sustained low-intensity pressure on Hezbollah, though no major escalation is evident.
sections.regional_response: Qatar's active mediation role underscores Gulf state interest in preventing wider conflict, while Flydubai's flight suspension reflects commercial sector risk aversion. The U.S. military options presentation to Trump signals Washington maintains credible strike capacity as diplomatic backup. Lebanese Army controlled demolitions suggest routine border security management rather than conflict escalation. No coordinated Gulf military posture changes are evident beyond diplomatic engagement.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Iranian missile tests from Isfahan and Khuzestan demonstrate geographic dispersal of launch capabilities, complicating preemptive targeting. The IRGC Fajr 19th Division tunnel activity in Fars may indicate hardening of strategic assets. The Israeli espionage case's use of Telegram groups for recruitment highlights social media vulnerabilities in military populations. Shin Bet's phone-based ultimatums to Hamas operatives represent a psychological warfare tactic that could accelerate internal fragmentation. Monitoring of Il-76 movements from Tehran may reveal supply routes to proxy forces.
